tasks.prompt: A new hilltop subdivision in Manitoba is designed to be fed from the existing zone, but its highest lots cannot reach adequate pressure even at night with no demand.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional subdivision in a Steinbach area system. Elevations were surveyed during design review after complaints from the first occupied high lots.

evidence.label: At zero demand at night, the highest lots read 170 kPa while the zone tank overflow sets a maximum possible head only 18 m above them.
Lower lots in the same subdivision hold 380 kPa at the same time.
Zone pressures elsewhere are normal and the tank is full.
Friction loss is near zero at night, so the shortfall exists with no flow at all.
The subdivision feed main and valves all test open and unobstructed.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The feed main is undersized and friction loss starves the high lots
A partly closed valve limits the subdivision at all hours
The tank level control is set too low for the whole zone
The highest lots sit too high for the existing zone head and need a separate higher zone or booster feed

inference.explanation: The shortfall exists at zero flow, so friction and a throttling valve cannot explain it, and the surveyed head above the lots is simply too small. The tank is full and the rest of the zone is normal, so this is an elevation and zone design limit, not an operating fault.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Upsize the feed main to the subdivision
Design a separate high zone or booster station for the top lots and keep the lower lots on the existing zone
Raise the whole zone pressure until the top lots are satisfied

nextClue.explanation: A dedicated high zone matches supply head to the surveyed elevations, which is the only fix for a static head shortfall.

clueText.nc-a: A larger main changes friction loss, which is already near zero in the failing condition.
clueText.nc-b: The design sets the new zone head to give the top lots about 350 kPa static, with the boundary at the surveyed contour.
clueText.nc-c: Raising the whole zone would overpressure every lower customer to serve a few high lots.

tasks.prompt: After routine maintenance at a pressure reducing station in a prairie city, the downstream zone runs 90 kPa high for a week before anyone notices.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional station in a Regina area system. The valve was serviced and returned to service by a two person crew.

evidence.label: Downstream pressure reads 440 kPa against a setpoint of 350 kPa, steady day and night.
Upstream pressure is unchanged at 620 kPa.
The valve responds when its setpoint is stepped in a test, moving downstream pressure up and down as directed.
Maintenance records show the setpoint dial was left at a test setting used during servicing.
No customer damage is reported, and zone demand is normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The valve was left at its servicing test setpoint instead of being returned to the zone setpoint
The valve has failed toward open and can no longer control
Zone demand fell and pressure rose naturally to 440 kPa
The upstream zone raised its pressure and pushed the zone up

inference.explanation: The valve still controls perfectly in the step test, upstream is unchanged, and the records show a test setting was left in place. A failed open valve would not follow setpoint steps, and falling demand cannot push pressure past a working valve setpoint.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the reducing valve with a new unit
Lower upstream zone pressure by 90 kPa
Reset the setpoint to 350 kPa, log the zone for a day, and add a setpoint verification line to the station return to service checklist

nextClue.explanation: Resetting and verifying the setpoint plus a checklist change fixes the proven human error and prevents its repeat at other stations.

clueText.nc-a: The valve passed its control test, so replacement is not warranted.
clueText.nc-b: Upstream pressure never changed, so lowering it would harm the upstream zone for no cause.
clueText.nc-c: The zone holds 350 kPa for the logged day and the checklist change is adopted for all stations.

tasks.prompt: Two pressure zones in a British Columbia town are joined by an intertie that should open on low pressure, but the upper zone still runs short during a large fire flow test.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional intertie with a check valve and a pressure sustaining control between zones in a Vernon area system. The fire flow test was planned and logged.

evidence.label: During the test, upper zone pressure falls to 140 kPa at the test hydrant.
Lower zone pressure stays at 480 kPa, so supply is available at the intertie.
Flow through the intertie is measured at near zero during the test.
The intertie check valve is later found seized shut with corrosion, and it frees with force in the shop.
When the check is removed in a second supervised test, intertie flow rises and upper zone test pressure improves greatly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lower zone refuses to share because its pumps are too small
The seized intertie check valve blocks support flow from the lower zone during high demand
The upper zone test hydrant is faulty and reads low
The intertie main is too small ever to help

inference.explanation: Lower zone pressure is ample, intertie flow is zero, the check is seized, and removing it restores support flow in a repeat test. Pump size and hydrant faults cannot explain zero intertie flow with a seized check in hand.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the check valve and add intertie exercise and flow testing to the annual program
Upsize the intertie main before retesting
Derate the upper zone fire flow requirement

nextClue.explanation: Replacing the failed check and testing the intertie yearly keeps an emergency support path proven, not assumed.

clueText.nc-a: The new check passes a flow test at the intertie and the upper zone repeat test meets its target.
clueText.nc-b: The main carried strong flow in the second test once the check was removed, so size is not the limit.
clueText.nc-c: Derating the requirement would hide a fixable failure in a safety support path.

tasks.prompt: A booster station and a pressure reducing valve serving the same Alberta neighbourhood fight each other: pressures oscillate whenever the booster runs.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional neighbourhood at a zone edge near Grande Prairie. The booster lifts water into the same streets the reducing valve feeds from the other side.

evidence.label: Oscillation starts within a minute of the booster starting and stops when it stops.
With the booster off, the reducing valve holds the neighbourhood steady at setpoint.
With the reducing valve station isolated in a trial, the booster holds pressure steadily on its own.
The booster discharge check and the reducing valve outlet are only 200 m apart on the same main.
Zone demand is steady during the oscillation tests.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both devices are individually faulty and need replacement
Neighbourhood demand oscillates and drives both devices
The booster and the reducing valve are hydraulically coupled on the same short main and each reacts to the other, so they cannot both control the same point
The pressure logger between them is picking up electrical noise

inference.explanation: Each device controls steadily alone and oscillates only together, with steady demand, which is the signature of coupled control rather than two independent faults. A logger fault would not stop and start with the booster in step with both device behaviours.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace both the booster controls and the reducing valve
Set one device to control and the other to a fixed support role, then log the neighbourhood through booster cycles
Accept the oscillation as unavoidable at zone edges

nextClue.explanation: Assigning a single controlling device removes the coupling that two successful solo tests identified.

clueText.nc-a: Both devices proved they can control alone, so wholesale replacement is not supported.
clueText.nc-b: With the reducing valve set as controller and the booster on fixed support, pressure holds steady through all cycles that week.
clueText.nc-c: Oscillation fatigues pipes and fixtures, and a proven control fix exists.

tasks.prompt: In midwinter in Thompson, Manitoba, a pressure zone drifts high for two days, then returns to normal during a warm spell without any adjustment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reducing valve station in a heated chamber, but its pilot sensing line runs through an unheated section of pipe chase. Northern Manitoba cold reached minus 38 C.

evidence.label: Downstream pressure rose to near upstream pressure during the coldest two days.
The valve did not respond to setpoint changes during the cold period.
Heat tracing on the pilot line chase is found tripped off, and the sensing line section is at below freezing temperature.
When the chase is warmed in a trial, the valve resumes control within an hour.
The same pattern occurred once the previous winter during a similar cold snap.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The valve diaphragm failed and then healed in warm weather
Customers used so little water in the cold that pressure rose to upstream level
The upstream zone pressure rose in the cold and pushed through a healthy valve
The pilot sensing line froze in the unheated chase, blinding the valve so it drifted open in the cold

inference.explanation: Loss of control tracks the cold exactly, the sensing line is found frozen with its heat trace tripped, and warming restores control within an hour. A diaphragm does not heal with weather, and a healthy controlling valve would hold setpoint regardless of low demand or upstream level.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the valve diaphragm every fall as a precaution
Lower the upstream zone pressure each winter
Restore and alarm the heat tracing, insulate the chase, and add pilot line freeze checks to the winter station routine

nextClue.explanation: Freeze protection and alarming address the proven cold weather failure mode for this station and similar ones.

clueText.nc-a: The diaphragm worked normally once the sensing line thawed, so it is not the fault.
clueText.nc-b: Upstream pressure was within its normal range during the event.
clueText.nc-c: With heat trace alarmed and the chase insulated, the valve holds setpoint through the next cold snap.

tasks.prompt: A Saskatchewan zone has good static pressure everywhere, but its far end drops sharply at peak while the station outlet at the zone entrance barely moves.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in a Swift Current area system fed by one long trunk main. Paired loggers were placed at the entrance and far end for a week.

evidence.label: Static night pressure is 410 kPa at both the entrance and the far end.
At evening peak, the entrance holds 395 kPa while the far end falls to 180 kPa.
The paired loggers show the gap grows with measured zone flow and shrinks to zero at night.
All trunk main valves are verified fully open.
Zone tank and pump supply at the entrance are proven adequate by the steady entrance pressure.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Friction loss in the long trunk main at peak flow is dropping the far end, so the limit is main capacity, not supply pressure
The entrance pressure gauge is faulty and the whole zone is actually low
A far end leak opens only at evening peak
The far end pressure reducing valve is failing closed

inference.explanation: Entrance pressure stays high, the gap tracks flow and vanishes at zero flow, and valves are verified open, which is the friction loss signature. A leak timed to peak and a failing valve are not supported, and the entrance gauge agrees with pump and tank records.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Use the paired logger data to size a trunk main upgrade or a far end booster for the capital plan
Replace the entrance pressure gauge and recheck in a month
Search the far end for a peak timed leak with acoustic survey

nextClue.explanation: Sizing the fix from measured loss against flow turns the diagnosis into a costed capital option, which is the Class 2 decision needed.

clueText.nc-a: The loss curve from the paired logs sizes a parallel main section that would hold far end peak pressure above 300 kPa.
clueText.nc-b: The entrance gauge was corroborated by two other instruments.
clueText.nc-c: Step and acoustic checks at peak found no leak flow to locate.

tasks.prompt: Customers at the bottom of a steep British Columbia zone complain of high pressure damage, while customers at the top of the same zone barely reach minimum pressure.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional single zone spanning 85 m of elevation in a Cranbrook area system. Pressures were surveyed at the top and bottom on the same day.

evidence.label: Bottom static pressure is 780 kPa and two pressure relief valves in homes have lifted.
Top static pressure is 215 kPa at the same hour with the tank full.
The difference between top and bottom matches the surveyed elevation difference closely.
No reducing or booster devices exist inside the zone today.
Both readings are steady and repeat on a second survey day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The tank level is set wrong and a single adjustment will fix both ends
One zone spanning 85 m cannot serve both ends well, so the zone needs to be split with its own control for the lower part
The bottom pressure gauge is faulty and damage reports are exaggerated
A leak at the top is pulling its pressure down

inference.explanation: Top and bottom readings are repeatable, their difference equals the elevation head, and relief valves lifting confirms the bottom is truly high. No single tank setting can move both ends in opposite directions, and a top leak would not create a difference that matches elevation exactly.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise the tank level to help the top and accept bottom pressure
Design a zone split with a reducing station feeding the lower part and a boundary at the mid elevation contour
Lower the tank level to help the bottom and accept top pressure

nextClue.explanation: Splitting the zone is the only option that lets each part be controlled near its proper pressure.

clueText.nc-a: Raising the tank worsens the bottom damage that relief valves already prove.
clueText.nc-b: The split design gives the lower part about 400 kPa and keeps the top at its current service level.
clueText.nc-c: Lowering the tank drops the top below minimum service pressure.

tasks.prompt: A zone in an Alberta city is normally fed by gravity from its tank, but operators find it running on direct pump pressure every morning with the tank still half full.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in a Medicine Hat area system. The tank altitude valve controls tank filling and the zone can also be fed by pumps through a check valve.

evidence.label: Morning zone pressure matches pump discharge pressure, not tank head, on most days.
Tank level sits near half each morning instead of cycling through its normal range.
The tank outlet check valve is found stuck partly shut with debris, limiting gravity outflow.
When the check is cleaned in a trial, the zone returns to tank head pressure and the tank cycles normally.
Pump run hours fall back to normal after the trial cleaning.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Morning demand is too high for gravity supply every day
The altitude valve is overfilling the tank each night
The partly stuck tank outlet check is forcing the zone onto pump supply and stalling tank cycling
Operators are choosing pump supply on purpose each morning

inference.explanation: The tank sits half full yet cannot supply, the outlet check is found fouled, and cleaning it restores gravity supply and normal cycling with lower pump hours. Overfilling contradicts a half full tank, and demand cannot explain a fouled check restoring flow when cleaned.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Add a larger pump to meet morning demand
Raise the tank overflow level to store more water
Clean and exercise the tank outlet check on a schedule and trend tank cycling range weekly

nextClue.explanation: Scheduled exercise plus cycling trends keep the gravity path proven, which protects both pressure stability and water turnover.

clueText.nc-a: Pumps already meet demand, and the fault was on the gravity path, not pump capacity.
clueText.nc-b: More storage height does not clear a fouled outlet check.
clueText.nc-c: Tank cycling range returns to its design band and stays there for the next quarter.

tasks.prompt: A reducing valve station in Saskatchewan was returned to service after repair, but the downstream zone now follows upstream pressure almost exactly at all hours.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional station in a Prince Albert area system with a valved bypass around the reducing valve. The bypass was used during the repair.

evidence.label: Downstream pressure equals upstream pressure minus a small steady difference at all flows.
Stepping the reducing valve setpoint produces no change downstream.
The station bypass valve is found one turn from fully open with its operating nut still fitted with the repair crew wrench.
Closing the bypass in a trial makes downstream pressure fall to the valve setpoint at once.
The reducing valve itself passed a bench response check during the repair.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The reducing valve failed again immediately after repair
Upstream pressure rose so high that the valve cannot reduce it
The downstream gauge now reads the upstream gauge line by mistake
The station bypass was left open after repair, short circuiting the reducing valve

inference.explanation: The valve passed its bench check, setpoint steps do nothing while the bypass is open, and closing the bypass restores control instantly. A repeat valve failure would not be cured by closing a bypass, and gauge cross connection would not respond to bypass closure either.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Close and verify the bypass, then add bypass position verification to the station return to service sign off
Send the reducing valve back to the shop for a second repair
Throttle the upstream zone feed valve to lower downstream pressure

nextClue.explanation: Bypass verification at sign off is the direct safeguard against the proven return to service error.

clueText.nc-a: With the bypass verified shut, the station holds setpoint through a week of logging.
clueText.nc-b: The valve already proved itself on the bench and again once the bypass closed.
clueText.nc-c: Throttling the zone feed would starve the upstream zone to mask a station error.

tasks.prompt: One pressure logger in a Manitoba zone reports nightly pressure spikes to 900 kPa, but no customer in the zone reports any problem and no relief valve has lifted.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in a Brandon area system with five loggers. Staff compared the suspect logger against a freshly calibrated test gauge at the same hydrant.

evidence.label: Four other loggers in the zone show a steady 380 kPa through the same nights.
A calibrated test gauge beside the suspect logger reads 385 kPa while it reports 900 kPa.
The suspect logger spikes occur at random minutes, not with any pump or valve event in station logs.
Swapping the suspect logger to another zone moves the spikes with the logger.
No pipe noise, damage, or relief valve discharge is found anywhere in the zone.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The single logger is faulty and the zone pressure is actually normal
The zone has real nightly surges that only one logger can detect
A hidden surge device operates at random minutes each night
All four other loggers and the test gauge are faulty together

inference.explanation: The calibrated gauge beside it reads normal, the spikes follow the logger to another zone, and nothing in the physical system matches a 900 kPa event. Four instruments and a test gauge agreeing cannot all be wrong in the same way, and a real surge would leave noise or damage.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Install surge protection across the zone based on the logger data
Remove the logger for repair and recalibrate the logger fleet on a set interval with field gauge checks
Instruct customers to expect nightly high pressure

nextClue.explanation: Logger calibration management fixes the data problem at its source and protects future pressure decisions from bad data.

clueText.nc-a: Surge work across the zone would spend heavily on an event no physical evidence supports.
clueText.nc-b: The repaired logger agrees with the test gauge within 10 kPa on its return check.
clueText.nc-c: Telling customers to expect surges that are not occurring would alarm them without cause.

tasks.prompt: A warm zone fed from a large storage tank in Alberta shows falling total chlorine, rising nitrite, and falling free ammonia over three weeks in August.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional chloraminated zone in a Lethbridge area system. Samples are taken at the tank outlet and at two zone sites on a set schedule.

evidence.label: Total chlorine at the tank outlet falls from 1.6 mg/L to 0.7 mg/L over three weeks.
Nitrite at the same sites rises from near zero to 0.08 mg/L over the same period.
Free ammonia falls steadily while nitrate edges upward.
Tank water temperature is 21 C and tank turnover has been low during a mild demand period.
Treatment plant effluent total chlorine and ammonia ratio leaving the plant are steady and on target.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant is underfeeding chlorine and the zone is simply reflecting it
Nitrification is underway in the warm, slow turning storage and zone water
The laboratory ammonia method has drifted for three weeks
A cross connection is diluting the zone with untreated water

inference.explanation: Plant effluent is steady and on target, so the change develops inside storage and the zone, and the combined pattern of falling total chlorine and free ammonia with rising nitrite is the nitrification signature. A lab drift would not move four related measures in a chemically consistent direction, and dilution would not raise nitrite.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise the plant chlorine dose and wait a month to recheck
Resample once next month to confirm the laboratory result
Increase tank turnover, flush the affected zone legs, and sample nitrite and total chlorine twice weekly until the trend reverses

nextClue.explanation: Turnover and flushing attack the warm old water where nitrification is established, and frequent sampling tracks whether the response is working.

clueText.nc-a: More plant chlorine is consumed by the nitrifying water before it can restore the far zone.
clueText.nc-b: Monthly resampling is far too slow for an active nitrification trend in warm water.
clueText.nc-c: Within two weeks of turnover and flushing, nitrite falls and total chlorine at the outlet recovers above 1.2 mg/L.

tasks.prompt: Free chlorine at the end of one dead end street in a Saskatchewan town reads 0.05 mg/L, while the main feeding the street reads 0.65 mg/L at the same hour.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional dead end in a Moose Jaw area system with six homes and a flushing hydrant at the end. Paired samples were taken on three days.

evidence.label: Street main samples at the dead end entrance hold 0.6 to 0.7 mg/L on all three days.
End of street tap samples hold 0.04 to 0.08 mg/L on all three days.
Flushing the end hydrant for ten minutes brings end samples up to 0.55 mg/L the same day.
By the next week without flushing, end samples fall back below 0.1 mg/L.
Homes on the dead end report no taste or odour problems, only the low residual is found.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The treatment plant residual leaving for this area is too low
The sample tap at the end home is contaminating every sample
Long water age in the low use dead end is consuming the residual before the end of the street
A leak at the end of the street is pulling in untreated groundwater

inference.explanation: Entrance samples are healthy, flushing restores the end at once, and the decay returns over days of low use, which is water age in the dead end. Plant residual cannot explain a healthy entrance reading, and a tap fault would not respond to hydrant flushing of the main.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Put the dead end on a scheduled flushing or auto flushing program and recheck residuals monthly
Raise the plant chlorine dose for the whole system
Replace the end home sample tap and stop sampling there

nextClue.explanation: Scheduled flushing controls water age where it occurs, keeping residual up without overdosing the whole system.

clueText.nc-a: On the flushing schedule, end of street residuals stay above 0.4 mg/L for the next two months.
clueText.nc-b: A system wide dose increase treats water that already holds residual well.
clueText.nc-c: The tap gave correct readings after flushing, so it was reporting the main condition faithfully.

tasks.prompt: Residuals across a whole British Columbia zone fall step by step over four days, starting the day its booster chlorination station ran out of chemical.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in a Kamloops area system with a booster chlorine station midway. Station chemical delivery records and zone sampling are available.

evidence.label: Zone entry residual stays at 0.9 mg/L from the plant all four days.
Residual just downstream of the booster station falls from 0.85 mg/L to 0.3 mg/L over the four days.
The booster chemical tank is found empty and its low level alarm had been muted during an earlier visit.
Far zone residuals fall a day later than near station residuals, in flow order.
Refilling the tank in a trial restores downstream residuals within a day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Plant chlorine production failed for the zone
Warm weather suddenly increased decay across the whole region
Zone demand rose and diluted the residual
The empty booster station stopped adding chlorine, so zone water decayed from the station onward

inference.explanation: Entry residual is steady, the fall begins at the booster station and moves downstream in flow order, and the tank is found empty with its alarm muted. Regional weather and plant failure cannot explain a fall that starts at one station with an empty tank.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Increase plant dose to cover the zone without the booster
Refill the station, restore and test the low level alarm, and add chemical level checks to the weekly station round
Sample the far zone daily and wait for residuals to recover alone

nextClue.explanation: Alarm restoration and routine level checks prevent the silent chemical outage that caused the zone wide fall.

clueText.nc-a: Plant dose cannot reliably replace a mid zone booster and would overchlorinate the entry area.
clueText.nc-b: With alarms tested, the next low level event pages the operator and the tank is refilled before it empties.
clueText.nc-c: Residuals cannot recover alone while the booster adds nothing.

tasks.prompt: Earthy taste complaints cluster in streets fed from one elevated tank in a Manitoba town, while plant treated water tastes normal and other tank areas report nothing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional town in a Steinbach area system with two elevated tanks. Complaint mapping and tank sampling were done over two weeks.

evidence.label: Complaints map tightly to the streets served by the north tank only.
Plant effluent samples show no taste or odour issue on the complaint days.
North tank turnover is very low: its level moves only a few percent each day in mild weather.
A sample drawn from the north tank itself carries the same earthy taste reported by customers.
The south tank, with daily cycling, produces no complaints and its sample tastes normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Water sitting too long in the slow turning north tank is developing the taste that customers report
The plant filters are failing and sending earthy water to the whole town
Customers near the north tank are imagining the taste after one report
A sewer cross connection is flavouring the north tank streets

inference.explanation: The taste is present in the tank sample itself, complaints map to that tank only, the paired tank with good turnover is normal, and plant water is clean. A plant failure would affect both tank areas, and a sewer connection would not present as a tank sample matching customer reports.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Change plant filter media based on the complaint cluster
Tell north tank customers the water is safe and take no action
Cycle the north tank through a wider level range and flush its outlet leg, then track complaints for two weeks

nextClue.explanation: Wider cycling reduces water age in the suspect tank, which is the variable that separates it from the healthy paired tank.

clueText.nc-a: Plant media is not implicated when plant samples are clean and one tank area is unaffected.
clueText.nc-b: The tank sample proved the taste is real, so dismissal would leave the cause running.
clueText.nc-c: Complaints stop within a week of wider cycling and the tank sample tastes normal again.

tasks.prompt: Brown water complaints in an Alberta neighbourhood spike on mornings after the zone tank drains for its weekly cleaning cycle test, then clear by midday.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional neighbourhood in a Grande Prairie area system. The tank drain test is a planned operation logged by staff.

evidence.label: Complaints occur only on test mornings and stop when the test schedule is paused for two weeks.
Hydrant samples on complaint mornings run brown at first draw, then clear with flushing.
Plant and zone entry water colour is normal on the same mornings.
The tank drain returns a high velocity flow through the neighbourhood feed main.
Streets not fed through that main report no discolouration on test mornings.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant sends brown water on test mornings by coincidence
High velocity return flow during the tank test stirs sediment in the feed main and discolours the neighbourhood supply
The tank is rusting inside and shedding colour every morning
Home water heaters across the neighbourhood fail on the same mornings

inference.explanation: Complaints follow the test schedule exactly, pause when it pauses, affect only streets on the return flow path, and clear with flushing. Plant water is normal at entry, and a rusting tank would colour water on non test days as well.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Slow the tank return rate during tests and flush the feed main after the next test to confirm complaints stay away
Replace the tank interior coating based on the complaint pattern
Advise customers to run taps every morning as a permanent routine

nextClue.explanation: Controlling return velocity tests the stirring explanation under the same operation that caused the complaints.

clueText.nc-a: With a slower return, the next two tests produce no complaints and hydrant samples stay clear.
clueText.nc-b: Coating work is not supported when discolouration follows a flow event, not the tank alone.
clueText.nc-c: Daily tap running wastes water to manage a cause the utility can control at the tank.

tasks.prompt: One routine sample site in a Saskatchewan city returns total coliform positive twice, while every other site in the zone is negative and residuals at the site are normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional site at an outdoor tap on a service yard in a Regina area system. Resampling followed the provincial drinking water requirements sampling procedure.

evidence.label: Free chlorine at the site is 0.55 mg/L on both positive days, in the normal zone range.
The outdoor tap is found with a submerged hose end in a wash bay drain area and a worn, dirty aerator style fitting.
Properly collected resamples from a cleaned, flamed style dedicated sample tap at the same service are negative three times.
Zone sites upstream and downstream are negative on all rounds.
Laboratory blanks and duplicates for the same batches are clean.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The zone has a real coliform intrusion that only this site detects
The laboratory contaminated both positive samples
The positive results come from the contaminated outdoor tap and hose arrangement, not from the distribution water
The service line to the yard is harbouring coliform growth that resamples missed

inference.explanation: Residual is normal, neighbouring sites are negative, lab quality checks are clean, and clean resamples from a proper tap at the same service are repeatedly negative, while the original tap is visibly compromised. A real intrusion would not vanish when only the tap and collection method change.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Flush and resample the whole zone repeatedly until all sites agree
Replace the site with a dedicated sample tap, keep the yard tap out of the program, and note the site change in the sampling plan
Issue a zone wide advisory based on the two positives

nextClue.explanation: Fixing the sample point protects the program from repeat false signals while keeping true surveillance in place.

clueText.nc-a: Zone flushing does not correct a tap that resubmerges a hose in a drain area.
clueText.nc-b: The new dedicated tap returns negative results on the next four routine rounds.
clueText.nc-c: An advisory is not supported when resamples, residuals, and lab checks all point to the tap.

tasks.prompt: Total coliform positives appear at four sites downstream of one ground reservoir in a British Columbia system over two weeks, with falling residuals at the same sites.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional system in a Prince George area community. The reservoir was returned to service three weeks earlier after an interior inspection.

evidence.label: All four positive sites are downstream of the reservoir, and no site upstream of it is positive.
Free chlorine at the four sites has fallen to 0.05 to 0.12 mg/L from a normal 0.5 mg/L.
Reservoir outlet residual is also low, while plant effluent residual is normal.
Laboratory blanks are clean and a second laboratory confirms the positive results.
The reservoir roof hatch is found with a damaged seal and bird droppings washed toward the opening after rain.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The laboratory is producing false positives for this system only
The plant is sending coliform positive water that upstream sites miss
Four sample taps failed in the same two weeks by coincidence
Contamination and residual loss are entering or developing at the reservoir, with the damaged hatch seal as a likely entry point

inference.explanation: Positives cluster only downstream of the reservoir, the outlet residual itself is low, results are confirmed by a second lab with clean blanks, and a damaged hatch seal with droppings is found. Upstream sites being negative rules out the plant, and four independent tap failures at once is not credible.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Resample the four taps with new fittings and keep the reservoir in service
Raise plant chlorine and wait for the positives to stop
Take the reservoir out of service for cleaning and hatch repair under the provincial requirements procedure, and resample its zone on the required schedule

nextClue.explanation: Removing the suspect reservoir from service addresses both the entry point and the low residual water it is supplying, which sampling alone cannot do.

clueText.nc-a: New tap fittings do not explain a low reservoir outlet residual.
clueText.nc-b: More plant chlorine is consumed before it reaches the zone and does not repair a hatch entry point.
clueText.nc-c: After cleaning and hatch repair, the reservoir returns with normal outlet residual and three clear resample rounds downstream.

tasks.prompt: Blue green staining and metallic taste complaints rise in one Alberta neighbourhood over two months after the plant adjusted its treated water pH downward for a trial.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional neighbourhood in a Lethbridge area system with mostly copper home plumbing. The pH trial is a logged plant change.

evidence.label: Complaints begin about two weeks after the pH change and grow steadily.
First draw samples in complaint homes show elevated copper compared with flushed samples from the same taps.
Street main pH in the neighbourhood reads 6.9, down from the historic 7.6.
Neighbourhoods held at the former pH in a paired zone show no rise in complaints.
No main breaks, construction, or source change occurred in the neighbourhood in the period.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Lower pH water is corroding copper plumbing in the neighbourhood, raising copper at first draw and causing the staining
Copper pipes in the neighbourhood all reached end of life in the same two months
A new subdivision upstream is leaching copper into the mains
Customers are confusing iron staining with copper staining

inference.explanation: The timing follows the pH change, first draw copper is elevated over flushed samples, street pH is measurably lower, and a paired zone at the old pH is unaffected. Pipe age does not change in two months, and iron staining does not produce elevated copper in first draw samples.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Restore the treated water pH target and monitor first draw copper and complaints in the neighbourhood monthly
Replace copper services across the neighbourhood
Flush the neighbourhood mains weekly until complaints stop

nextClue.explanation: Restoring pH corrects the water chemistry that the paired comparison identifies as the driver of corrosion.

clueText.nc-a: Within two months of restoring pH, first draw copper falls and staining complaints return to baseline.
clueText.nc-b: Services are not the variable that changed, and the paired zone with the same pipes is unaffected.
clueText.nc-c: Flushing does not change the pH of water standing in home plumbing overnight.

tasks.prompt: A unidirectional flushing program in a Manitoba city restores residuals in most areas, but one pocket stays low no matter how long crews flush its hydrant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional pocket of streets in a Winnipeg area system. The flushing plan requires a specific valve sequence to drive high velocity flow from a clean source.

evidence.label: Flushing the pocket hydrant for two hours produces only low velocity flow and residual stays at 0.1 mg/L.
Neighbouring pockets flushed the same week reach target velocity and their residuals recover.
A valve on the planned clean water feed path to the pocket is found closed, though the plan shows it open.
Opening that valve in a trial raises hydrant velocity sharply and residual climbs to 0.5 mg/L during the flush.
The pocket mains are the same age and material as the neighbouring pockets that recovered.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pocket mains have a chlorine demand no flushing can overcome
The closed feed valve prevents the flushing program from driving clean high velocity water through the pocket
The flushing crew is using the wrong hydrant in the pocket
The pocket needs a permanent booster chlorine station

inference.explanation: Same age mains recovered next door, the planned feed valve is found closed against the plan, and opening it restores both velocity and residual in the trial. An insurmountable wall demand would not yield to a valve position change, and the crew flushed the planned hydrant throughout.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Install a booster chlorine station in the pocket
Correct the valve position, reflush the pocket on the plan sequence, and add valve verification to the flushing setup checklist
Flush the pocket hydrant for a full day at low velocity

nextClue.explanation: Valve verification in the setup checklist makes the proven failure mode part of every future flushing setup.

clueText.nc-a: A booster would dose water that proper flushing already restores.
clueText.nc-b: On the corrected sequence, the pocket reaches target velocity and holds residual above 0.4 mg/L the following month.
clueText.nc-c: A full day at low velocity still cannot scour or replace water the way the designed sequence does.

tasks.prompt: Chlorine residual decays far faster in one old cast iron reach of a Saskatchewan system than in a new plastic reach carrying the same water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional paired reaches in a Saskatoon area system, both fed from the same main on the same days. Travel times through the two reaches are similar.

evidence.label: Entry residual to both reaches is 0.80 mg/L on test days.
After similar travel time, the plastic reach exits at 0.68 mg/L while the cast iron reach exits at 0.25 mg/L.
The cast iron reach shows heavy tuberculation in a cut out coupon from a recent repair.
Water temperature and flow are similar in the two reaches during tests.
Flushing the cast iron reach improves its exit residual for a day, then decay returns to the fast rate.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The cast iron reach has a large leak diluting its water
The plastic reach is receiving extra chlorine from somewhere
The tuberculated cast iron wall exerts a high chlorine demand that consumes residual in that reach
The sample bottles for the cast iron reach are faulty

inference.explanation: Both reaches start with the same water at the same residual, temperature and travel time match, and the only material difference is the tuberculated wall, whose coupon is in hand. A leak would show in flow balance, and faulty bottles would not track a one day flushing improvement.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise entry residual for the whole system until the cast reach complies
Stop sampling the cast iron reach exit
Include the reach in the lining or renewal program and use interim targeted flushing to hold its exit residual

nextClue.explanation: Renewal planning addresses the wall demand at its source, while interim flushing manages residual in the reach that needs it.

clueText.nc-a: System wide increases overchlorinate healthy reaches to compensate for one reach.
clueText.nc-b: Ending sampling hides a known residual problem instead of managing it.
clueText.nc-c: The reach is ranked for lining, and interim flushing holds its exit residual above 0.4 mg/L between flushes.

tasks.prompt: Residual loss in a British Columbia zone is severe every August and mild every January, with the same mains, valves, and plant dose in both seasons.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in a Kelowna area system with long summer water temperatures near 23 C and winter temperatures near 4 C. Two years of seasonal sampling are available.

evidence.label: Far zone residual averages 0.15 mg/L in August and 0.55 mg/L in January.
Entry residual is held at 0.9 mg/L in both seasons by the plant.
Zone water age estimated from tank cycling is similar in both seasons.
The pattern repeats in both years of records.
Flushing restores August residuals for about a week, much less time than the same flushing lasts in January.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The zone develops a large leak every August that seals every fall
Plant operators lower the dose every August without recording it
August samples are mishandled in the heat every year
Warm summer water temperature is driving much faster chlorine decay in the zone

inference.explanation: Entry dose is constant, water age is similar, the pattern repeats yearly, and flushing benefit decays faster in August, all of which point to temperature driven decay. A seasonal self sealing leak and unrecorded dose cuts are contradicted by the steady entry residual records.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Adopt a seasonal residual program with summer booster or dose review and more frequent far zone sampling in warm months
Replace zone mains to fix the August residual pattern
Sample only in winter when residuals pass easily

nextClue.explanation: A seasonal program matches effort to the proven temperature effect instead of treating August as a surprise each year.

clueText.nc-a: The next August holds far zone residuals above 0.35 mg/L under the seasonal program.
clueText.nc-b: New mains would still carry warm water that decays chlorine faster.
clueText.nc-c: Winter only sampling would miss the season when the risk actually occurs.

tasks.prompt: In a chloraminated Alberta storage tank, total chlorine still reads a moderate 1.1 mg/L, but staff suspect nitrification is starting and debate whether to act early.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank in a Calgary area system sampled weekly at inlet, outlet, and a depth profile point. The utility tracks nitrite and free ammonia as early indicators.

evidence.label: Free ammonia at the outlet has fallen for four straight weeks while inlet ammonia is steady.
Nitrite at the outlet has risen from 0.005 mg/L to 0.03 mg/L over the same four weeks.
Tank temperature has climbed to 19 C as summer arrived.
Total chlorine has drifted down only slightly, from 1.25 mg/L to 1.1 mg/L.
Turnover has been low because demand is being carried by a second tank.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Early nitrification is starting in the tank, shown by ammonia loss and nitrite rise before total chlorine collapses
The tank is healthy because total chlorine is still above 1.0 mg/L
The nitrite rise is a laboratory error repeated for four weeks
The inlet water chemistry changed and the tank is only reflecting it

inference.explanation: Inlet chemistry is steady while outlet ammonia falls and nitrite rises in a consistent multi week trend in warming, slow turning water. That is the early nitrification pattern, and waiting for total chlorine to collapse ignores the indicators the program collects for this purpose.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Wait until total chlorine falls below 0.5 mg/L before acting
Raise turnover through this tank, flush its outlet leg, and move to twice weekly nitrite and ammonia checks until the trend reverses
Ask the laboratory to recheck its nitrite method and take no field action

nextClue.explanation: Early turnover and monitoring act while the process is still reversible with operational measures.

clueText.nc-a: Waiting for collapse allows nitrification to establish and become much harder to reverse.
clueText.nc-b: Two weeks of higher turnover bring nitrite back down and stabilize free ammonia.
clueText.nc-c: Four weeks of consistent paired trends are not explained by a single method error.

tasks.prompt: A booster chlorine station in Manitoba holds residual well on weekdays, but the zone downstream fades every weekend and recovers every Monday.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional station in a Winnipeg area system with a dosing pump sized for weekday industrial demand. Station run logs are tied to a flow switch.

evidence.label: Weekend zone flow falls to a third of weekday flow.
Station logs show the dosing pump runs very few hours on weekends because its flow switch needs higher flow to trigger.
Downstream residual falls from 0.7 mg/L on Friday to 0.2 mg/L by Sunday night each week.
On a trial weekend with the pump set to a low continuous rate, downstream residual holds near 0.6 mg/L.
Chemical supply and pump condition test normal on weekdays.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Weekend customers use water that has no chlorine in it from a separate source
The flow triggered dosing control starves the zone on low flow weekends because the pump rarely runs
The pump is wearing out and fails only on weekends
Sunday samples are always stale because of the sampling schedule

inference.explanation: The pump and chemical system work on weekdays, logs show the flow switch rarely triggers on weekends, and a continuous low rate trial holds residual through the weekend. Wear does not follow a calendar, and the trial result rules out a sampling artifact.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the dosing pump with a larger weekday sized unit
Sample only on weekdays when residuals are good
Change the station control to flow paced dosing with a low flow trim, and log weekend residuals for a month

nextClue.explanation: Flow paced control with a low flow trim matches dose to the full range of real flows, not just weekday peaks.

clueText.nc-a: A larger pump triggered by the same switch would still sit idle at weekend flows.
clueText.nc-b: Weekday only sampling would hide the exact period the station was failing.
clueText.nc-c: Weekend residuals hold above 0.55 mg/L for the month after the control change.

tasks.prompt: A home in a Saskatchewan town consistently samples low for chlorine, yet the street main in front of the home samples normal on the same days.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional home in a Yorkton area system with a very long service line and a whole home treatment unit. Paired sampling was done at the curb stop, the home entry, and the kitchen tap.

evidence.label: Curb stop samples read 0.60 mg/L on all test days.
Home entry samples before the treatment unit read 0.45 mg/L, lower after the long service run.
Kitchen tap samples after the treatment unit read 0.05 mg/L.
Bypassing the treatment unit in a trial brings the kitchen tap to 0.42 mg/L.
Neighbouring homes without treatment units sample 0.5 to 0.6 mg/L at their taps.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The street main is failing to deliver chlorine to this block
The home service is cross connected to a well
The home treatment unit is removing chlorine, and the long service adds some decay, so the street supply itself is normal
The kitchen tap sample bottles were all faulty

inference.explanation: Curb samples are normal, neighbours are normal, and bypassing the unit restores the tap reading, which isolates the loss to the home equipment with a smaller service line decay step. A main failure cannot produce a normal curb reading at the same home.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Record the site as a premise plumbing case, sample the program site at the curb or a neighbour tap, and advise the owner about the unit removing residual
Flush the street main weekly for this one home
Raise the zone chlorine dose until this kitchen tap complies

nextClue.explanation: Program sampling belongs on the distribution water the utility controls, and the owner advice addresses the in home cause.

clueText.nc-a: Program records move to a representative tap and the owner service call closes the complaint with the bypass result explained.
clueText.nc-b: Street flushing cannot change what a home unit removes after the meter.
clueText.nc-c: Raising zone dose to satisfy one treatment unit would overchlorinate every other customer.

tasks.prompt: After a new booster chlorine pump is installed at a British Columbia station, downstream residuals overshoot for two days, then crash below normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional station in a Vernon area system. The new pump is a different model with its own stroke and speed settings, commissioned by a contractor.

evidence.label: Commissioning records show the pump was set by copying the old pump dial numbers.
The new pump delivers twice the volume per stroke of the old model at the same dial setting.
Chemical tank level fell twice as fast as normal during the overshoot days.
When the tank emptied, downstream residual crashed, and the low level alarm had not been reconnected after the install.
Plant and zone entry residuals stayed normal throughout.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Zone demand doubled for two days and then vanished
The chemical supplier delivered double strength product for one tank
Downstream samplers mishandled samples in both directions
The uncalibrated replacement pump overdosed until it emptied the tank, then the zone lost boosting entirely

inference.explanation: Tank drawdown at twice the normal rate, a pump with twice the stroke volume set by copied dial numbers, and an unconnected alarm explain both the overshoot and the crash in sequence. Demand and product strength stories cannot explain the stroke volume mismatch found in the equipment records.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Return to the old pump model without checking settings
Calibrate the pump output by drawdown test, reconnect and test the alarm, and add output verification to the pump replacement procedure
Double the chemical delivery frequency and accept the dose swings

nextClue.explanation: Drawdown calibration sets dose by measured output, which is the step the replacement skipped.

clueText.nc-a: Any replacement pump still needs output calibration, whatever its model.
clueText.nc-b: After calibration, the station holds downstream residual within its target band for a month.
clueText.nc-c: More deliveries feed an uncalibrated dose faster without fixing control.

tasks.prompt: A chlorine like taste complaint wave hits one Alberta zone in the week after its storage tank was returned to service following disinfection after maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in an Airdrie area system. The tank was disinfected, flushed, and sampled before return under the utility procedure.

evidence.label: Complaints begin the day the tank returns and fade over the following week.
Free chlorine at zone taps near the tank reads 1.8 mg/L on return day, against a normal 0.6 mg/L.
Tank outlet samples on return day also read high and decline steadily each day.
Bacteriological samples from the tank before return were satisfactory and zone samples since return are satisfactory.
Zones not fed by this tank report no taste change.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residual disinfection water left in the tank raised chlorine in its zone until the tank water turned over
The plant overdosed the whole system that week
The tank coating is leaching a chlorine flavoured chemical
Customers are reacting to news of the maintenance, not the water

inference.explanation: High readings are measured at the tank outlet itself, only its zone is affected, safety samples are satisfactory, and levels decline with turnover exactly as stored disinfection water would clear. A plant overdose would lift all zones, and a coating leach would not decline steadily with turnover.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Recoat the tank interior before its next return to service
Lower plant chlorine for a week to compensate
Flush or blend down the first tank volume on return procedures and verify outlet residual is in the normal band before full return

nextClue.explanation: Checking outlet residual before return catches stored disinfection water while it can still be managed at the tank.

clueText.nc-a: Coating is not implicated when levels fall steadily with turnover and safety samples pass.
clueText.nc-b: Lowering plant dose does not remove the high chlorine volume already stored in the tank.
clueText.nc-c: The revised return checklist holds the next return until outlet residual reads within the normal band, with no complaints.

tasks.prompt: An elevated tank in a Saskatchewan city cycles only between 92 and 100 percent full, and the zone it serves shows rising water age and falling residuals.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank in a Regina area system with level controls set years ago when a second tank carried more of the load. SCADA level trends cover three months.

evidence.label: Level trend shows the tank refills as soon as it drops 8 percent and stops at full, every day.
The second tank that once shared the load is out of service for a long repair.
Zone residuals far from the tank have drifted down as the shallow cycling continued.
Inlet and outlet flows are both active daily, so the tank is not valved off.
A trial widening of the control band to 60 to 100 percent raises daily exchange and residuals recover within two weeks.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The tank outlet is blocked and only a small volume can move
The narrow control band exchanges too little water each day, so most of the tank volume sits and ages
The level sensor is stuck near full and the tank actually cycles widely
Zone demand is too low ever to cycle any tank

inference.explanation: Flows move daily, the trial band change immediately increases exchange and restores residuals, and the shallow band is visible in three months of trends. A blocked outlet would not respond to a setpoint band change, and a stuck sensor would not change real residuals when the band changes.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Keep the wider control band and trend weekly exchange volume and far zone residual together
Replace the level sensor and return to the old band
Take the tank out of service to force the zone onto pumps

nextClue.explanation: Keeping the proven band and trending exchange against residual makes turnover a managed operating target.

clueText.nc-a: Exchange volume stays in the new range and far zone residuals hold their recovered level for the quarter.
clueText.nc-b: The sensor reported the change the band trial produced, so it was working.
clueText.nc-c: Removing storage harms fire protection and pressure stability to solve a setpoint problem.

tasks.prompt: Summer samples from the top of a ground reservoir in British Columbia differ sharply from samples at its outlet, and the outlet residual fades on hot afternoons.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir in a Kamloops area system with a mechanical mixer that was switched off during an electrical repair. Temperature and residual profiles were taken at three depths.

evidence.label: Top water is 6 C warmer than bottom water on profile days.
Top residual reads 0.75 mg/L while bottom and outlet residual read 0.25 mg/L.
The mixer control is found switched off with the electrical repair tag still attached.
Restarting the mixer in a trial evens the profile within a day and outlet residual recovers.
Inlet flow and plant residual entering the reservoir are steady and normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant residual is failing on hot afternoons
The outlet sample tap is faulty on hot days only
With the mixer off, the reservoir stratified, and the outlet draws the warm, low residual bottom layer
Sunlight is destroying chlorine through the reservoir roof

inference.explanation: Entry residual is steady, the depth profile shows real stratification, the mixer is found off with its repair tag, and restarting it evens the profile and restores the outlet. A tap fault would not produce a full depth profile or respond to mixing.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Raise plant residual on hot afternoons to cover the outlet
Return the mixer to service, add mixer status to the reservoir weekly check, and profile the reservoir each summer
Draw the reservoir down and refill it every hot week

nextClue.explanation: Mixer status checks keep the proven stratification cause from silently returning after future repairs.

clueText.nc-a: Extra plant chlorine still enters a stratified tank whose bottom layer is the problem.
clueText.nc-b: Profiles stay uniform through the rest of the summer with the mixer running.
clueText.nc-c: Weekly drawdowns waste storage and do not fix a mixer left off.

tasks.prompt: An elevated tank in northern Manitoba reports erratic level readings all winter, and its overflow pipe discharged twice on nights when pumps were already off.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank in a Thompson area system with a roof vent and an overflow. The tank riser and vent were inspected from the roof hatch in spring.

evidence.label: Level readings jump up and down by a metre between scans on calm nights.
Ice is found capping the roof vent and partly blocking the overflow screen in spring.
During the coldest weeks, air pressure effects are noted: water is pushed from the tank when mild air returns after deep cold.
The level instrument passes a bench calibration test in spring.
Pump and valve records show no filling during the two overflow nights.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The level instrument failed intermittently all winter
Pumps secretly ran on the overflow nights despite their records
The tank shell developed a winter leak that sealed in spring
Ice blocking the vent trapped air in the tank, causing false level behaviour and pushing water out the overflow as air pressure changed

inference.explanation: The instrument calibrates fine, pumps are proven off, and ice is found capping the vent and overflow, which explains both erratic readings and pressure driven discharge. A shell leak would lose water steadily, not discharge through the overflow on mild nights.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace the level instrument with a different technology
Lower the tank operating level for the whole winter
Add vent and overflow ice inspection to the fall winterization round and fit a vent design suited to severe icing

nextClue.explanation: Winterization checks target the icing failure mode that northern operation makes predictable.

clueText.nc-a: The original instrument passed calibration, so technology was not the fault.
clueText.nc-b: A lower level reduces storage all winter without clearing a blocked vent.
clueText.nc-c: The next winter passes with stable level readings and no overflow events after the vent work.

tasks.prompt: A ground reservoir in Alberta overflows on quiet nights about once a month, wasting treated water, while its level chart looks normal at the daily reading time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir in a Red Deer area system filled through an altitude valve. Overnight SCADA trends were reviewed after a wet area was noticed by the overflow drain.

evidence.label: Overnight trends show level creeping past the stop point to overflow on the event nights.
The altitude valve closes very slowly and sometimes stops a few percent short of shutoff on test cycles.
Daytime filling behaves normally because demand draws the level down before overflow is reached.
The overflow drain area is wet only after the quiet night events.
Level instruments agree with a manual tape measurement on event mornings.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The altitude valve is failing to close fully on low flow nights, so the reservoir creeps to overflow
Night operators are overfilling the reservoir on purpose monthly
The level instrument drifts high at night and the overflow is rainwater
Groundwater is entering the reservoir and raising its level

inference.explanation: Valve tests show incomplete closure, instruments agree with tape readings, and overflow follows quiet nights when nothing draws the level down. Groundwater entry would be continuous and would raise quality concerns not seen in sampling, and the wet drain follows the level trend, not rainfall.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Service the altitude valve, function test full closure at low flow, and set a high level alarm below the overflow
Raise the overflow pipe to gain more storage
Instruct night staff to watch the reservoir hourly

nextClue.explanation: Valve service plus a high level alarm fixes the closure fault and catches any repeat before water is wasted.

clueText.nc-a: Low flow closure tests pass after service and no overflow occurs in the following quarter.
clueText.nc-b: Raising the overflow does not stop a valve that cannot close and risks the roof structure.
clueText.nc-c: Hourly watching treats a mechanical fault as a staffing duty and will eventually miss a night.

tasks.prompt: A standpipe in a Saskatchewan town stops supplying its zone during a January cold snap, though it was filled the week before and no break is found.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional standpipe in a Humboldt area system with a narrow riser pipe. Temperatures held below minus 30 C for ten days.

evidence.label: Zone pressure falls to pump only supply while the standpipe level gauge reads nearly full.
A test flow from the standpipe base drain starts as a trickle of slush and slowly improves as milder water circulates.
Heat tracing on the riser is found failed, with the pipe chase at ambient cold temperature.
Neighbouring storage with working heat trace cycles normally through the same cold snap.
After the riser thaws under supervision, the standpipe returns to normal cycling.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The standpipe emptied through an undetected leak
Ice formed a plug in the unheated riser, isolating the full standpipe from its zone
The level gauge froze at a false full reading while the tank is empty
The zone outgrew the standpipe capacity that week

inference.explanation: The gauge reads full, thawing restores service, the riser heat trace is found failed, and a paired storage with working heat trace is unaffected. An empty tank would not return to service by thawing a riser, and demand growth does not reverse with a thaw.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Insulate the whole standpipe shell more heavily
Repair and alarm the riser heat tracing and add standpipe flow verification to cold snap rounds
Keep the standpipe out of service every winter

nextClue.explanation: Alarmed heat tracing protects the narrow riser, which is the proven freeze point, while flow checks catch any repeat early.

clueText.nc-a: Shell insulation does not protect the exposed riser chase where the plug formed.
clueText.nc-b: Flow checks through the next cold snap confirm the riser stays open with the tracing alarmed.
clueText.nc-c: Winter removal of storage leaves the zone without its fire and peak reserve in the highest risk season.

tasks.prompt: A two cell reservoir in British Columbia returns low residuals from one cell only after both cells are put back in service following cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional reservoir in a Kelowna area system where both cells share an inlet but have separate outlets. Cell sampling was done at each outlet.

evidence.label: Cell A outlet residual reads 0.55 mg/L and Cell B outlet reads 0.12 mg/L on the same days.
A dye test in Cell B shows dye reaching the outlet in under an hour, far faster than the cell detention time.
Cell B inlet and outlet are at the same corner of the cell with no baffle between them.
Cell A has a baffle wall and its dye test travels the full cell before exiting.
Both cells receive the same inlet water at the same residual.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Cell B water is being contaminated by a cracked wall
Cell B outlet sample tap is faulty
Cell B short circuits from inlet to outlet, so most of its volume sits old while a stream of new water slips through
The cleaning crew left disinfectant absorbing material in Cell B

inference.explanation: Same inlet water gives two different outlets, and the dye test proves a fast path in the unbaffled cell while the baffled cell behaves normally. A tap fault would not change a dye travel time, and contamination would not present as a detention time failure.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Clean Cell B again and return it without changes
Blend Cell B outlet with Cell A and stop cell sampling
Fit baffling or reconfigure Cell B inlet and outlet separation, and verify with a repeat dye test

nextClue.explanation: Baffling corrects the flow path the dye test measured, and the repeat test proves the fix in the same terms as the diagnosis.

clueText.nc-a: Recleaning does not move an inlet that sits beside its outlet.
clueText.nc-b: Blending hides a cell whose stored volume is aging unmonitored.
clueText.nc-c: After baffling, Cell B dye travel approaches its design detention and outlet residual matches Cell A.

tasks.prompt: A Manitoba town tank level sensor reports the tank full all week, yet zone pressure sags every evening and recovers when pumps are run manually.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank in a Portage la Prairie area system with a pressure based level sensor in a stilling well. The stilling well is exposed to winter cold.

evidence.label: The sensor output does not change for six days while pump logs show water moving in and out.
A manual tape from the roof hatch shows the tank actually cycling between 40 and 70 percent.
Ice is found bridging the stilling well, isolating the sensor from the tank water surface.
Evening sags occur because automatic filling trusts the false full signal and does not start pumps.
Clearing the ice in a trial makes the sensor track the tape readings at once.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The tank really is full and the evening sag is a pump fault
The manual tape measurement is wrong because of roof ice
Zone demand doubled for exactly one week
Ice in the stilling well froze the level signal, so controls believed a cycling tank was always full

inference.explanation: The tape shows real cycling, pumps respond when run manually, and clearing stilling well ice restores a tracking signal immediately. A full tank cannot sag nightly from lack of filling, and the tape and sensor agree once the ice is cleared.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Protect and heat the stilling well, add a sensor versus pump flow plausibility check to SCADA alarms
Replace the pumps for failing to fill a full tank
Trust the sensor and investigate zone demand instead

nextClue.explanation: Plausibility alarming catches a frozen signal by comparing it with flows, which protects every winter night, not just this one.

clueText.nc-a: The plausibility alarm catches a brief refreeze the next month before pressure is affected.
clueText.nc-b: Pumps filled correctly whenever they were actually called to run.
clueText.nc-c: The sensor was the element proven wrong by tape and by its recovery after clearing.

tasks.prompt: Two elevated tanks serving one Alberta zone behave unequally: one cycles daily while the other barely moves and its zone corner shows low residuals.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional zone in a Leduc area system with two tanks of different overflow elevations. Level trends and a survey of both overflow levels are available.

evidence.label: Tank 1 overflow is surveyed 1.2 m lower than Tank 2 overflow.
Tank 1 fills and spills slightly on high fill nights while Tank 2 never reaches its top range.
Tank 2 level moves only a few percent daily and its outlet residual is the lowest in the zone.
Both tank outlet valves are verified fully open.
Equalizing the operating levels in a trial, by lowering Tank 1 control level, makes Tank 2 begin cycling.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The overflow elevation difference makes Tank 1 dominate, so Tank 2 stagnates until operating levels are balanced
Tank 2 outlet is blocked and cannot exchange water
Tank 2 has a large leak that keeps it from filling
Customers near Tank 2 use almost no water

inference.explanation: Outlets are open, Tank 2 holds its level rather than losing it to a leak, and the surveyed elevation difference plus the successful balancing trial explain the dominance. A blockage would not respond to lowering the other tank control level.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Replace Tank 2 outlet piping to clear the suspected blockage
Reset control levels to balance exchange between the tanks and trend both cycling ranges monthly
Accept Tank 2 as a standby tank and sample it yearly

nextClue.explanation: Balanced control levels keep both storages turning over, which protects residual across the whole zone.

clueText.nc-a: The outlet was verified open and carried flow once levels were balanced.
clueText.nc-b: Both tanks cycle through healthy ranges the following month and Tank 2 outlet residual recovers.
clueText.nc-c: A stagnant in service tank is a water quality risk, not a standby asset, under this program.

tasks.prompt: A reservoir in a Saskatchewan system loses more water overnight than the district uses, but only in weeks when a nearby construction dewatering program is running.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional covered reservoir in a Saskatoon area system. Overnight balance tests were repeated with construction dewatering on and off.

evidence.label: Overnight loss beyond district use is 180 cubic metres on dewatering weeks and near zero on other weeks.
A crack inspection finds a floor joint that weeps when the surrounding water table is drawn down by dewatering.
Reservoir water quality samples stay satisfactory and the loss stops when the floor joint is temporarily sealed in a test patch.
District meters and the outlet meter reconcile on non dewatering weeks.
No overflow or drain flow occurs on loss nights.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Construction crews are taking reservoir water at night
Dewatering lowers groundwater support and opens a floor joint leak path that the reservoir loses water through
The outlet meter under reads only on dewatering weeks
Evaporation increases when construction lights are on

inference.explanation: The loss follows dewatering on and off, a weeping joint is found, and sealing it in a test stops the loss, while meters reconcile in normal weeks. Night taking would not stop with a floor patch, and evaporation from a covered reservoir cannot reach this volume.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Meter a construction standpipe and close the case
Raise reservoir level at night to offset the loss
Programme a permanent floor joint repair for the next cell outage and monitor overnight balance during any nearby dewatering

nextClue.explanation: Repairing the joint removes the loss path, and balance monitoring during dewatering verifies the repair under the condition that caused it.

clueText.nc-a: A standpipe meter does not explain a loss that a floor patch stopped.
clueText.nc-b: Higher level increases head on the leaking joint and would lose more water.
clueText.nc-c: During the next dewatering program after repair, overnight balance stays within normal limits.

tasks.prompt: Taste complaints and low residuals trace to one tank in a British Columbia system, and its inspection finds several centimetres of sediment across the floor.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional tank in a Vernon area system last cleaned nine years ago. A sister tank cleaned two years ago serves a neighbouring zone with no complaints.

evidence.label: Complaints and low residuals map only to streets served by the suspect tank.
Diver inspection photos show deep sediment and the outlet sample carries higher turbidity than the inlet sample.
The sister tank zone with recent cleaning has normal residuals and no complaints.
Plant effluent and zone entry samples are normal on complaint days.
After cleaning in a planned outage, the tank outlet residual and turbidity match its inlet within a month of return.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The plant is sending sediment laden water to this tank only
The tank roof is leaking soil into the water
Sediment accumulated in the long uncleaned tank is exerting demand and degrading its stored water quality
Customers near this tank have more sensitive taste than the sister zone

inference.explanation: Entry water is normal, the paired recently cleaned tank is healthy, inspection shows the sediment, and cleaning restores outlet quality. A plant source would affect the sister tank too, and a roof leak would not be cured by floor cleaning alone producing a full recovery.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best confirms the explanation and guides the fix?

options.label: Set a risk based tank cleaning and inspection interval from this record and schedule the fleet by years since cleaning
Clean this tank only when complaints return
Raise plant chlorine to overcome the sediment demand
